title: Disease detection and classification in temporal lobe epilepsy: step-wise versus simultaneous AI decision models in a multisite neuroimaging study
summary: A multisite study of 3,676 participants across 26 sites found that a staged model strategy—first detecting temporal-lobe epilepsy, then lateralizing the focus—performed better than simultaneous detection and lateralization. This is a retrospective neuroimaging result; it does not establish prospective clinical decision benefit.
ai_technology: AI models classify temporal lobe epilepsy and lateralize the epileptogenic focus from neuroimaging using sequential or simultaneous decisions.
organization: Department of Radiation Medicine and Applied Sciences, University of California San Diego, La Jolla,; Halıcıoğlu Data Science Institute, University of California San Diego, La Jolla,; Department of Mathematics and Statistics, San Diego State University, San Diego,; Department of Neurology, Emory University, Atlanta

evidence.tested: The study compared sequential and simultaneous AI decision strategies across 26 sites and 3,676 participants.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective multisite evaluation; prospective workflow impact and patient outcomes were not assessed.
